answer: Each agent must stake a walnut-sized hardware token whose unique key is registered on-chain; forging identities then requires buying and physically securing scarce tokens, so mass sybil creation costs real capital and logistics. Peers randomly challenge tokens during epochs, and the system reaches its security zenith when honest stake outweighs attackers' sunk costs. Like a single ocean absorbing countless rivers, one verified identity per token prevents cheap duplication, making large-volume sybil farming economically irrational.
